claims.text: Adding a controlled amount of boron to refractory high-entropy alloys improves their high-temperature mechanical capability.
Boron addition limits the density of the modified refractory high-entropy alloy.
Boron addition preserves room-temperature mechanical performance.
Boron addition produces boride precipitates in the refractory high-entropy alloy.
Dislocation pinning by boride precipitates enhances high-temperature strength.
Dislocation pinning by boride precipitates enhances creep resistance.
Boride precipitation does not significantly compromise room-temperature ductility.
Relative to the boron-free baseline alloy, boron addition increases high-temperature yield strength by at least 10%.
Relative to the boron-free baseline alloy, the density reduction after boron addition is less than 2%.
Boron addition causes only minimal degradation of room-temperature tensile properties.
The hypothesized benefit applies above 1000°C and up to 1200°C under stresses relevant to jet-turbine operation.

contradictions.description: The prediction requires at least a 10% yield-strength improvement, but the experiment falsifies the hypothesis only below 5%. An improvement from 5% to less than 10% would violate the stated prediction without falsifying the hypothesis.

The predicted outcome specifies a density reduction of less than 2%, whereas the falsification rule permits a density increase of up to 2%. Thus, a small density increase could contradict the directional prediction without triggering falsification.
